div.head: IV Eg 12.1
div.ab: ⁊ þæs wilnige, þæt þes án dóm on swylcere smeagunge sy ús eallon gemæne, to gebeorge ⁊ to friðe eallum leodscipe.
⁊ ðæs wilnige, þæt ðes án dom on swylcere smeagunge sy ús eallon gemæne, to gebeorge ⁊ to friðe eallum leodscype.
⁊ ðæs wilnige þæt ðes án dom on swylcere smeagunge sy ús eallon gemæne, to gebeorge ⁊ to friðe eallum leodscype.
Jedoch das wünsch ich, dass dies eine [obige] Gesetz über solche Untersuchung uns allen gemeinsam sei, zu Schutz und zu Sicherheit allem Volke.
But this I desire, that this one [above] law on such inquiry be common to us all, for the protection and security of all the people.
But I desire that this one decree relating to investigations such as these shall apply equally to us all, for the protection and security of the whole population.
And I desire that this one decree concerning such an investigation shall be common to us all, for the protection and security of all the nation.
div.note: Not in the Latin Versio. In F, ‘þæs’ was changed by the scribe from ‘þæt’. Liebermann compares IV Eg 2.2 ff.

note.seg: altered by the scribe from þæt
Nicht ‘search for stolen (lost) cattle’ [Toller], sondern nach dem unbekannten Eigentümer ertappten, verdächtigen Viehs
Not ‘search for stolen (lost) cattle’ [Toller], but search for the unknown owner of suspicious cattle that has been detected
Including the Northmen; thus as in 1, 6. 2, 2. 14, 2

This is interpreted as referring to the search for the stolen cattle (see BT. p. 887, s.v. smeagung) or else to the inquiry for the unknown owner of the suspected cattle which have been seized (Liebermann). Does it not refer to the whole process of investigation with regard to cattle which have not been reported?
